Canasta Rules

Classic Canasta for two players with 108 cards, as played here.

The rules

Cards and deal
108 cards: two packs of 52 and four jokers. Each player gets 15 cards; the next card is turned up as the discard pile (a joker, Two or red Three stays in the pile and the next card is turned).
A turn
Draw two cards from the stock or take the whole discard pile. Then lay out melds if you like, and end by discarding one card.
Melds
At least three cards of one rank (Four to Ace), at least two of them natural, at most three wild cards. You have only one meld of each rank; more cards of that rank are added to it.
Wild cards and Threes
Jokers and Twos are wild. A red Three is laid out at once (dealt or drawn) and replaced from the stock; it counts 100 points (all four 800). A black Three blocks the pile for the next player and can only be melded when going out.
First meld
The cards of your first meld must count at least 50 points - 15 with a negative score, 90 from 1500, 120 from 3000. Values: joker 50, Ace and Two 20, Eight to King 10, Four to Seven and black Three 5.
Taking the pile
The top card must go straight into a meld: with at least two cards from your hand, or onto your meld of its rank. Before your first meld it needs two natural cards of its rank, and it counts towards the minimum.
Frozen pile
While a wild card (or a red Three from the start) lies in the pile, it is frozen: the top card can only be taken with two natural cards of its rank. A black Three or a wild card on top can't be taken.
Canasta
A meld of seven or more cards: natural canasta (no wild card) 500 points, mixed canasta 300.
Going out
You go out when you have no cards left - by melding all of them or by discarding the last one. You need two canastas for that (two-player rule). Going out brings 100 points, going out concealed (all melds in one turn) 200.
Empty stock
When the stock is used up, a player who can take the discard pile must; otherwise the hand ends. A red Three as the last card also ends it.
Score
The cards in your melds, canasta bonuses, red Threes and going out count for you; the cards left in your hand count against you. Without a meld the red Threes count against you.
End of the game
The game ends when a player has 5000 points (short game: 2000) after a hand; the higher score wins.
PaperGames rules
The top card is taken together with the melds that use it, so taking the pile can't go wrong. Going out concealed also needs the minimum for the first meld.

Example

A mixed canasta of Kings: five Kings, a Two and a joker - seven cards, worth 50 + 20 + 50 = 120 points plus 300 for the canasta.
